title: Soma told me: in the waters are all remedies

sandhi_exceptions.note: सोमो अब्रवीत्: -o before a- inside a pāda is left unjoined in the Veda (P. 6.1.115 (प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे)).

sandhi.rule: m before c is written as the palatal nasal ñ (or anusvāra)

samasa.meaning: a source of welfare for all

morphology.note: the accusative depends on abravīt understood: Soma told of Agni too.

translation.literal: Soma told me: within the waters are all remedies, and Agni, beneficial to all; and the waters are the remedy of all.
translation.readable: Soma has told me that within the waters lie all remedies — and Agni, who blesses all — and that the waters are a remedy for all things.

meaning: An anuṣṭubh verse in praise of the waters: Soma himself has said that every remedy lies within the waters, together with Agni who is good for all, and that the waters are the remedy of all things. The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa has it at 2.5.8; it is also Ṛgveda 1.23.20, in a hymn to the waters. The commentary in the sources does not discuss this verse. The verse names Soma, and Soma speaks in it. The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Soma’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, in praise of the Waters. S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre anuṣṭubh. The Ṛgveda (1.23.20) has the same words in two lines.

notes.label: direct
notes.text: No commentary on this verse is in the edition’s sources: the Brāhmaṇa commentary file for TB 2.5.8 does not comment on it, so none is quoted.
